title: Loki
description: Loki on loki01-03 (RF 3, chunks in the Ceph RGW bucket loki) and the Alloys that feed it: health checks mirroring the logging alerts, ingestion and discards, ingesters, chunks and WAL, the ring, queries, S3, compactor and retention, ruler, every Alloy sender, resources.

panels.title: VIPs on
panels.description: The log VM holding keepalived's VIPs (10.13.11.101 for Grafana and the Alloy pushes, 10.5.11.101 for syslog from the devices; one VRRP instance, they move together). Its Alloy receives the devices' syslog and its distributor most pushes.

panels.title: Compactor
panels.description: The instance the compactor ring elected (a single token): only it compacts the index and applies retention (90d).

panels.title: Checks
panels.description: Mirrors the logging alert group (logging.tf): TargetDown, LokiRingMembersMissing (fewer than 3 ACTIVE ingesters), LokiRingUnhealthy, LokiIngesterFlushFailures and AlloyLokiWriteDrops (over the last 15 min), SyslogIngestStopped, RGWBackendDegraded/Down (haproxy on every log VM sees all 3 RGWs) and LoggingVIPNotHeldOnce per VIP. 'retention ran' is no alert: the compactor applies retention every compaction_interval (10 min).

panels.title: Lines received/s
panels.description: Log lines all distributors accept per second (before the ingesters drop duplicates: the dns and proxy VMs push to all three Lokis).

panels.title: Bytes received/s
panels.description: Uncompressed line bytes the distributors accept per second.

panels.title: Streams in memory
panels.description: Active streams (unique label sets) held by an ingester. With RF 3 and three ingesters each holds every stream, so this is the max of the three.

panels.title: Bucket loki (RGW)
panels.description: Chunks and TSDB index in Ceph (RGW bucket stats from the Ceph mgr). Grows until the 90d retention starts deleting.

panels.title: Since last retention run
panels.description: Since the elected compactor last applied retention successfully (it marks chunks older than 90d; the sweeper deletes them after retention_delete_delay, 2 h).

panels.title: Discarded in range
panels.description: Lines Loki refused in the time range, summed over the three Lokis (a line the ingesters refuse is counted by each replica). Reasons in Ingestion > Discarded lines by reason.

panels.title: Loki instances
panels.description: One row per Loki. VIPs: holds the keepalived VIPs. Compactor: the elected one. Lines/s: what its distributor accepts (pushes land on the VIP holder, each log VM's own Alloy on its local Loki). Streams/Chunks: in its ingester's memory. Flush queue: chunks waiting for S3 (should be 0). RGWs UP: healthy RGWs its haproxy sees. Ruler groups: rule groups the ruler ring gave it (one group, 'logging', on one of the three).

panels.title: Received per distributor
panels.description: Lines (left) and bytes (right axis) each distributor accepts per second. Structured metadata: per-line key/values outside the labels.

panels.title: Push requests (HTTP /loki/api/v1/push)
panels.description: Pushes from the Alloys by HTTP status (204 = accepted; 429 = rate limited; 500 = the ingesters didn't answer: Alloy retries 5xx/429 with backoff and drops the batch after its last retry) and the p99 latency (right axis).

panels.title: Discarded lines by reason
panels.description: Lines per minute Loki refused. too_far_behind: older than its stream's newest line minus max_chunk_age/2 (an out-of-order sender: a device whose clock is behind, or a resend after a VIP move); every ingester counts it, so the three hosts show the same lines. rate_limited / per_stream_rate_limit: over ingestion_rate_mb 16 / the per-stream limit (the push gets a 429).

panels.title: Lines stored by host (Loki)
panels.description: From Loki itself (LogQL over every stream): lines per bucket of the 15 busiest hosts, after the duplicate copies were dropped. The monitoring and service VMs log their journal (source=journal), the devices and PVE nodes syslog. Logs overview has the lines.

panels.title: Bytes stored by source (Loki)
panels.description: Log bytes per bucket: syslog (network devices, PVE nodes) vs the VMs' journals. LogQL over every stream, so a long range takes a few seconds.

panels.title: Distributor → ingester appends
panels.description: Push batches each distributor sends to each ingester (by ring address: 10.21.12.34-36 = loki01-03 on VLAN 214). With RF 3 every batch goes to all three; a write succeeds once two answer. Timeouts: an ingester that didn't answer in time (restart, overload).

panels.title: Bytes per line
panels.description: Size of the lines pushed (all distributors; bucket boundaries are powers of 2, so the quantiles are coarse).

panels.title: Ingester push (gRPC)
panels.description: Push requests each ingester gets from the distributors, by result (429: the ingester's per-stream limit), and their p99 latency (right axis).

panels.title: Streams in memory
panels.description: Active streams per ingester, and churn (dashed, right axis): a stream is created on its first line and removed once its chunks are flushed and it went idle. High churn means a label with many values (e.g. a per-request id) in the stream labels.

panels.title: Chunks in memory and flush queue
panels.description: Open and not yet flushed chunks per ingester, and chunks queued for upload to S3 (right axis). The queue should drain to 0 within seconds; a growing queue means S3 (haproxy, RGW) is slow or failing.

panels.title: Chunks flushed by reason
panels.description: Chunks per minute (selected ingesters) by why they were cut: idle (stream quiet for chunk_idle_period, 30 m), max_age (2 h), full (target size reached), synced. Mostly idle/max_age = many small streams. FAILED: alert LokiIngesterFlushFailures.

panels.title: Chunk utilisation and size at flush
panels.description: Mean fill of the flushed chunks against the target chunk size (1.5 MB), and their mean compressed size (right axis). Low utilisation is expected here: most streams are quiet and get flushed idle or at max_age.

targets.expr: sum by (host) (rate(loki_ingester_chunk_utilization_sum{job="loki", host=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (host) (rate(loki_ingester_chunk_utilization_count{job="loki", host=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

sum by (host) (rate(loki_ingester_chunk_size_bytes_sum{job="loki", host=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (host) (rate(loki_ingester_chunk_size_bytes_count{job="loki", host=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Chunk age and entries at flush
panels.description: How long a chunk was open when it was flushed, and how many lines it held (right axis).

targets.expr: sum by (host) (rate(loki_ingester_chunk_entries_sum{job="loki", host=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (host) (rate(loki_ingester_chunk_entries_count{job="loki", host=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Chunk bytes stored / compression
panels.description: Compressed chunk bytes each ingester writes to S3 per second (every ingester flushes the same chunks: three writes of one object), and the mean compression ratio (right axis).

targets.expr: sum by (host) (rate(loki_ingester_chunk_compression_ratio_sum{job="loki", host=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (host) (rate(loki_ingester_chunk_compression_ratio_count{job="loki", host=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: WAL writes
panels.description: What each ingester appends to its write-ahead log (/var/lib/logging/loki/wal, the VM's root disk) so unflushed chunks survive a restart. Records/s on the right axis.

panels.title: WAL disk usage
panels.description: Usage of the filesystem the WAL is on (the VM's root disk; Loki reports 0-1). Above wal.disk_full_threshold (90 %) the ingester stops writing the WAL and keeps data in memory only.

panels.title: Checkpoints
panels.description: A checkpoint writes every in-memory chunk to the WAL dir so the log segments before it can be deleted (every 5 min; Loki spreads the writes over the interval, so ~4 min is normal).

panels.title: WAL problems in range
panels.description: Corrupt WAL records skipped at replay, WAL writes skipped because the disk was full, failed checkpoints, and whether an ingester is replaying its WAL right now (after a restart; it isn't ready until done).

panels.title: Ring members by state
panels.description: Members of each Loki ring by state, as seen by the Loki that sees fewest. Every ring should list 3 ACTIVE and 0 elsewhere; LEAVING/JOINING during a restart, Unhealthy = missed heartbeats (alert LokiRingUnhealthy; ingester ring below 3 ACTIVE: LokiRingMembersMissing).

panels.title: memberlist
panels.description: Gossip members each Loki sees on VLAN 214 (3 expected), and its memberlist health score (right axis; 0 = healthy, rises when it misses probes, e.g. a CPU-starved VM).

panels.title: Ring KV updates and errors
panels.description: Ring state updates (heartbeats, token changes) and what went wrong: failed compare-and-swap on the ring key, packets the TCP transport couldn't send to a peer, gossip messages dropped.

panels.title: Query requests by route
panels.description: Requests to Loki's query API per route (Grafana panels, Explore, Logs Drilldown's volume and patterns): they arrive on the VIP holder's frontend.

panels.title: Query latency p99 by route
panels.description: End-to-end time of the query API requests at the frontend. Range queries over days of every stream (the log dashboards' totals) take seconds.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, route) (rate(loki_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="loki", host=~"$instance", route=~"loki_api_v1_.+", route!="loki_api_v1_push"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Query errors by route and status
panels.description: Failed query requests per minute. 499/cancel = the client gave up (a dashboard refreshed or closed before the answer); 400 = a bad LogQL expression; 429 = query limits; 5xx = Loki failed.

targets.expr: sum by (route, status_code) (rate(loki_request_duration_seconds_count{job="loki", host=~"$instance", route=~"loki_api_v1_.+", route!="loki_api_v1_push", status_code=~"[45]..|cancel"}[$__rate_interval])) * 60 > 0

panels.title: LogQL execution latency by type
panels.description: Per executed (sub)query, by kind: filter = log lines, metric = count_over_time & co., limited = plain selector, series/volume/stats = metadata. p50 dashed.

panels.title: Data processed by queries
panels.description: Bytes per second a query scans (decompressed), and chunks fetched from the store per querier (right axis). The newest data (not yet flushed) comes from the ingesters, the rest from S3.

panels.title: Scheduler queue and caches
panels.description: Queries waiting in the query scheduler and sub-queries the queriers run; and the hit ratio of Loki's embedded caches (chunks, results; right axis).

targets.expr: sum by (name) (rate(loki_cache_hits{job="loki", host=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (name) (rate(loki_cache_fetched_keys{job="loki", host=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: S3 requests by operation
panels.description: Requests the selected Lokis send to S3 (through the local haproxy) per operation: PutObject = chunk flushes and index uploads, GetObject = queries and index sync, List = index tables, DeleteObject = retention. ERROR: non-2xx answers.

panels.title: S3 latency by operation
panels.description: Time to the RGWs and back, per operation (Ceph RGW on macbeth/titania/venom). Mean dashed.

targets.expr: sum by (operation) (rate(loki_s3_request_duration_seconds_sum{job="loki", host=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (operation) (rate(loki_s3_request_duration_seconds_count{job="loki", host=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: haproxy → RGWs
panels.description: Each log VM's haproxy (127.0.0.1:7480) and the three RGWs behind it: healthy servers (alerts RGWBackendDegraded below 3, RGWBackendDown at 0), mean response time of its last 1024 requests (right axis) and 5xx answers.

panels.title: Bucket size
panels.description: The bucket loki in Ceph (RGW bucket stats, before replication). Grows until the 90d retention catches up (the schema started 2026-11-01). Objects on the right axis.

panels.title: Index (TSDB) uploads and syncs
panels.description: Per hour: each ingester ships its TSDB index files to S3, and each querier syncs the index tables it needs from S3. A failure status means that window's index may be missing from S3 until the next upload.

panels.title: Chunk store traffic
panels.description: Chunk bytes each Loki writes to and reads from the store (written = flushes; fetched = queries reaching past the ingesters).

panels.title: Elected compactor
panels.description: Which Loki ran the compactor when. Exactly one should be green at a time; it moves when that VM restarts.

panels.title: Since last successful run
panels.description: Age of the last successful index compaction and retention pass (the newest over all three, so a standby's old timestamp doesn't count). A saw-tooth up to ~10 min (compaction_interval) is normal; a line that keeps rising means the compactor is stuck or failing.

panels.title: Compactor operations
panels.description: Runs per hour by result, how long the last retention pass took (right axis), and log delete requests (Grafana / API deletes) waiting to be processed.

panels.title: Rule evaluation
panels.description: The 'logging' group (RouterOSBGPNoBFD, SataLinkReset, KernelDiskIOError, KernelHardwareError) runs on the ruler that owns it in the ruler ring. Duration of its last evaluation; failed rules and skipped iterations (evaluation slower than the interval) per hour, right axis.

panels.title: Alerts sent to Alertmanager
panels.description: Alert notifications per hour, per Alertmanager (both get every alert; the cluster dedups). Only the ruler that evaluates the group sends, and only while a log alert is firing.

defaults.noValue: No log alerts sent in range

panels.title: Alloys
panels.description: Every Alloy that ships logs. Pushes to: Loki endpoints it writes to (1 = the VIP or its local Loki; 3 = the dns and proxy VMs, which push to all three Lokis over mgmt). Entries/s: lines it pushes (one endpoint's count). Dropped: entries it gave up on (alert AlloyLokiWriteDrops; reason ingester_error = Loki answered 5xx until the last retry). Config: last reload of config.alloy succeeded. Unhealthy components: pipeline components not healthy.

targets.expr: sum by (host) (alloy_component_controller_running_components{job="alloy", host=~"$sender", health_type!="healthy"}) or max by (host) (up{job="alloy", host=~"$sender"}) * 0

panels.title: Entries pushed per sender
panels.description: Lines each Alloy pushes per second (for the dns/proxy VMs one endpoint's count: the other two carry the same lines). The log VMs' own Alloys carry the devices' syslog as well as their journal.

panels.title: Dropped, retried and failed pushes
panels.description: Per bucket: entries dropped after the last retry, batch retries, and pushes Loki answered with something other than 2xx (429 limit, 500 ingesters, -1 = no answer, e.g. during a VIP move or a Loki restart).

panels.title: Push latency and entry delay
panels.description: Push p99: one HTTP push to Loki. Entry delay p99 (dashed): from the line's timestamp to its push, which includes batching, retries and, for syslog, the sender's clock.

panels.title: Sources: journal and syslog
panels.description: Lines each Alloy reads: its VM's journal, and on loki01-03 the syslog listeners (the VIP holder gets the devices; mgmt-VRF senders spread over all three). Parse errors: a sender whose format the listener can't parse (move it to the raw UDP 1514 listener). SyslogIngestStopped fires when all syslog stops for 15 min.

panels.title: Loki CPU
panels.description: CPU cores used by each Loki process (100 % = one core).

panels.title: Loki memory
panels.description: Resident memory and Go heap in use (dashed). Streams, chunks and the embedded caches live in the heap.

panels.title: Alloy CPU (top 10)
panels.description: The busiest Alloys (100 % = one core). The log VMs parse syslog as well as their journal.

panels.title: Alloy memory (top 10)
panels.description: Resident memory of the largest Alloys.

panels.title: Log VMs: CPU and memory
panels.description: loki01-03 as a whole (Loki, Alloy, haproxy, node_exporter, keepalived). Memory dashed.

panels.title: Log VMs: root FS used
panels.description: The WAL, TSDB index cache, compactor working dir and ruler WAL live on / (/var/lib/logging/loki); chunks are in S3. Alert FilesystemAlmostFull.

targets.expr: 1 - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{job="node", role="logging", mountpoint="/"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{job="node", role="logging", mountpoint="/"}

panels.title: Loki warnings and errors per instance
panels.description: Loki's own warn/error lines (the level= in the line: the journal marks all of Podman's stderr as err). 'context canceled' errors are queries the client abandoned.

targets.expr: sum by (host, lvl) (count_over_time({app="loki", host=~"loki0[0-9]"} | regexp `level=(?P<lvl>[a-z]+)` | lvl=~"warn|error" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Alloy warnings and errors per VM
panels.description: Alloy's own warn/error lines on every VM: failed pushes, syslog listener problems, reloads.

panels.title: Loki warnings and errors
panels.description: Without the 'context canceled' noise of abandoned queries.

panels.title: Alloy warnings and errors
panels.description: Alloy's warn/error lines from every VM's journal.
